item.title: World War II with Tom Hanks
item.description:
A new show has been added to showRSS: World War II with Tom Hanks.

For eighty years, the Second World War has remained the most devastating and defining conflict in human history. World War II with Tom Hanks is a landmark documentary event that reexamines the war through the lens of a new century. Told over twenty hours and guided by Tom Hanks, whose lifelong passion for this history has shaped some of the most profound screen portrayals of the era, the series captures the full arc of the war — from the rise of fascism in Europe to the fall of Berlin, from Pearl Harbor to Hiroshima, and the uneasy peace that follows. Each episode uncovers new dimensions of the conflict: the decisions that shaped the battlefield, the unseen networks that sustained the war effort, and the aftershocks that still shape our world today. "World War II with Tom Hanks" is the definitive retelling of that story for a new generation: a sweeping, deeply human portrait of how the modern world was forged in the fires of global war.

For decades, the North Andhra region watched from afar as cities like Hyderabad grew rapidly.
Today, the Bhogapuram International Airport is finally a reality, but it has triggered a fierce credit war between two political titans: #chandrababu Naidu and Jagan Mohan Reddy. Who actually deserves the credit for this mega-project? Did Naidu's early vision lay the foundation, or did Jagan's execution of the "middle stretch" make it happen?. We break down the paper trail, the controversies, and the final verdict.
Before Bhogapuram Airport could take flight, it faced a massive legal hurdle. In 2016, farmers approached the High Court, questioning why the land acquisition layout looked like a twisted "Octopus" instead of a standard square. Why were specific real estate plots excluded? This controversy led to a High Court stay and forced the government to drastically shrink the project. Discover the early real estate battles that almost killed the airport.

Yet, years later as Chief Minister, he took ownership of the project. Why the sudden reversal? We dive into how the project was scaled down to 2,200 acres , how the GMR deal was finalized, and the truth behind the initial land acquisition controversies.
The MANSAS trust, chaired by Ashok Gajapathi Raju, donated 136 acres of prime real estate next to the #bhogapuramairport to the #gmrgroup for an #aviation training campus. Supporters call it a royal charity meant to generate jobs for North #andhrapradesh youth. Critics argue it was a calculated business strategy to skyrocket the value of surrounding lands owned by the trust and secure long-term influence.
